rounds.proof_sketch: cg::reduce returns the same value to ALL 32 threads in the warp. Original: thread 0 writes warp_sum to block_sums[warp_idx]. Mutated: threads 1-31 write warp_sum to block_sums[warp_idx]. Same value written to same location → identical behavior.
rounds.survival_reason: The cooperative_groups reduce function broadcasts its result to all participating threads. After the warp reduction, every thread in the warp holds the identical warp_sum value. The mutation changes which threads perform the write (thread 0 vs threads 1-31), but since they all write the same value to the same shared memory location, the stored result is identical. CUDA guarantees that multiple threads writing the same value to shared memory produces that value. The block.sync() ensures proper synchronization. Layer 2's 112-round bitwise equivalence testing confirms this analysis.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under any value pattern because the semantic equivalence stems from the cg::reduce function broadcasting the same result to all threads in the warp, making it irrelevant which threads perform the write.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing tools should recognize that cooperative_groups reduction operations broadcast results to all threads, making mutations that change which thread writes the result semantically equivalent when all writing threads have the same value.
